messages:
dina: Heads up — after the NF4/FP4 canary push to a small pod pool we see a ~30% throughput drop and intermittent GPU memory spikes on the canaries. Not full OOMs but sustained >80% GPU mem then spills. Root cause guess: kernel selection is picking an FP4 microkernel for some NF4 layers.

raj: saw this too. timelines: drop started ~09:12 UTC when canary config `quant_profile: mixed_nf4_fp4` rolled to ~5% traffic. Logs show repeated 'kernel fallback' messages and a lot of KV cache evictions.

tom: can you paste the selector log lines? also which workload distribution (seq len dist)?

dina: seq dist is mostly 64-256 tokens with a small tail. selector excerpt: 
```
[2026-11-12 09:12:18] kernel-selector INFO selected kernel=fp4_rv32 for layer=encoder_11 model=redwood-nf4-v2 threshold=0.62
[2026-11-12 09:12:18] kernel-selector WARN mismatch quant=NF4 expected_kernel=nf4_rv16 selected=fp4_rv32
[2026-11-12 09:12:20] runtime INFO KVCache: eviction_rate=0.18 hold_ratio=0.67
```

sylvie: that WARN line looks suspect — selector probably uses a heuristic that considers perf benchmarks but not memory layout for KV. FP4 kernels use a different block packing and sometimes increase kv footprint for past-key storage. That could explain evictions.

raj: agreed. profiler (pprof) from canary heap shows hot path is `kv_write_batch` and `kernel_dispatch_slowpath`. Flamegraph attached (gcloud link): https://perf.redwood.dev/flames/2837771122/slot1

infra-bot: deploy canary quant_profile=mixed_nf4_fp4 to pool=canary-pool-17 finished (id=deploy-20261112-0911).

tom: hypothesis: kernel-selector scoring function optimizes latency per-op but misses overall system pressure from larger KV sizes + microbatch alignment changes. Two interacting regressors: 1) selector picks fp4 kernel for some matmuls that are slightly faster in isolation but allocate larger temporary buffers; 2) batching heuristic changed prefill window and caused more 1-token microbatches which degrade amortized perf and increase mem churn.

dina: repro steps I ran locally (small sim):
```bash
# simulate canary load profile
./loadgen --model redwood-nf4-v2 --quant mixed_nf4_fp4 --seq-dist 64,256 --qps 120 --concurrency 16 --trace=kv
```
Output shows steady 28% throughput drop vs baseline quant=NF4-only.

raj: can we quickly force kernel_selector to prefer nf4 kernels for that model as a mitigation? I can push a selector override to the canary pool.

sylvie: yes but we should also capture a minimal reproducer and a pprof of the selected fp4 kernel’s workspace alloc pattern. I think fp4 kernel backend does per-thread temp arena that scales with blocksize param. If NF4 uses a smaller block, memory wins even if single-op latency is higher.

tom: action items:
- raj: flip selector override to prefer `nf4_*` for redwood-nf4-v2 on canary pool (short rollback if no improvement)
- dina: run the simulated load with `KV_PREFILL=disabled` and `microbatch_align=16` to see if batching alignment is the other factor
- sylvie: grab pprof heap and cpu for an affected canary pod and upload flamegraph link
- infra-bot: schedule telemetry snapshot (token breakdown + per-pod mem hist) at 09:30 UTC

raj: I'll push override now: `PATCH /selector/config {"model":"redwood-nf4-v2","prefer":"nf4"}`. applying to canary-pool-17...

infra-bot: selector config patched (patch-id=sel-patch-9921) target=canary-pool-17.

raj: quick check after override: throughput recovered ~18% within 60s, KV eviction rate down to 0.03. Not back to baseline yet but moving in right direction.

dina: nice. I ran the two local sims: with `KV_PREFILL=disabled` throughput improved another 6%, and forcing `microbatch_align=16` removed most small batch churn. So both selector and batching heuristics were amplifying the regression.

sylvie: uploaded pprof links: CPU: https://perf.redwood.dev/pprof/2837771122/cpu ; Heap: https://perf.redwood.dev/pprof/2837771122/heap . Heap shows many `kv_slot` allocations pinned to fp4 kernel calls.

tom: long-term fixes: update kernel-selector scoring to include a memory pressure penalty (live KV footprint estimate) and add an integration test that runs mixed-quant workloads with representative seq distributions. Also we should add a guard in runtime that prevents selecting kernels with >X% increase in working-set vs model baseline when KV occupancy >Y.

raj: I'll draft the scoring change: new score = latency_score + lambda_mem * est_kv_delta + lambda_temp * temp_alloc_delta. Start with lambda_mem=0.8 and iterate.

dina: +1. Also we should revert canary override after selector patch lands to validate automated selection picks the right kernel.

infra-bot: telemetry snapshot complete (id=tele-2837771422). Summary: canary-pool-17 avg latency +22%, percentiles degraded, KV evictions correlated to kernel switch windows.

sylvie: I'll open a PR with profiler artifacts and a small unit test to assert selector avoids high-kv kernels under pressure. PR will include the reproducer loadgen script and the profiling outputs.

tom: thanks all. follow-up meeting at 10:15 to review selector change and rollout plan. :thumbsup:
